target.title: feat(cli): add openclaw promos to discover and claim ClawHub promotional model offers
target.body:
Closes #100234

### What Problem This Solves

ClawHub publishes time-boxed promotional model offers (`GET /api/v1/promotions`), but existing OpenClaw users have no way to activate one short of re-running onboarding or hand-editing config — and no way to *learn about* one without reading an announcement. Offers expire on a schedule, so activation must be fast and must not require an OpenClaw release per promotion.

### Why This Change Was Made

Adds an `openclaw promos` command group (`list`, `claim <slug>`) that turns a claim into a ~30-second flow, plus **passive discovery** riding ClawHub's hosted promotions feed, while treating all remote payloads as strictly declarative:

- Every remote identifier is contract-validated at the parse boundary (`src/infra/clawhub.ts`): slug (`[a-z0-9-]`), model refs (shell-safe, must start with the promotion's declared provider), provider/authChoiceId (identifier grammar), pluginNames (npm package-name grammar, scoped names allowed). Display text is `sanitizeTerminalText`-ed at output. A malformed or compromised promotion cannot make the CLI execute anything, print terminal controls, or emit unsafe copy-paste commands.
- Auth reuses existing machinery end-to-end: unknown auth-choice ids are refused with an "update OpenClaw" message (manifest choices first, install catalog second — mirroring `applyAuthChoiceLoadedPluginProvider`); existing provider credentials are reused only when the provider plugin is actually installed; otherwise the provider's normal auth-choice flow runs (install + enable + auth), with completion revalidated before any config write. `--api-key` follows the shipped `onboard --<provider>-api-key`/`--token` non-interactive contract; provider env vars work with no flag at all.
- Models register through the canonical config mutators (`upsertCanonicalModelConfigEntry`); aliases are held to the `models aliases add` contract and never overwrite existing aliases; plugin enablement is enforced (policy-blocked plugins refuse the claim); setting the suggested default is offered — never forced — and runs the same Codex/Copilot runtime-plugin repair as `openclaw models set`.
- **Passive discovery** (`src/infra/promotions-feed.ts`, `src/commands/models/list.promotions.ts`): a cadence-gated (24h), fail-silent conditional GET of ClawHub's immutable feed snapshot (`GET /api/v1/feeds/promotions`, wire contract `clawhub-promotions` schemaVersion 1, `If-None-Match` → `304`), cached in the shared state DB (two new SQLite tables — no new files) fully separate from `update_check_state` so promo discovery can never delay or break update checks. `models list` then renders an "Available via promotion" group for live offers whose models are not configured (reading only the cache, never the network), tags claimed models `promo` / `promo ended` from claim provenance recorded at claim time, and prints a one-time notice per newly seen offer (suppressed after `promos list`/`claim`, and entirely absent in `--json`/`--plain`). Snapshot sequence is monotonic — a stale edge can never roll the cache back. `promos claim` still always revalidates against the live API, so ClawHub's kill switch wins regardless of feed staleness.
- Zero new config keys, env vars, or state files (state lives in the existing shared SQLite state DB).

### User Impact

Existing users see live offers directly in `openclaw models list` (with a claim command), can run `openclaw promos list` for details, then `openclaw promos claim <slug>` (optionally `--api-key`/`--set-default` for non-interactive use) and immediately use promotional models. Models claimed through a promotion are tagged `promo`, flipping to `promo ended` when the window passes so users learn why a model stopped serving. Nothing about their defaults, aliases, or credentials changes without explicit consent; machine outputs stay clean. Docs: `docs/cli/promos.md` (incl. new passive-discovery section).

### Evidence

- Unit tests: 46 across `src/commands/promos/claim.test.ts` (claim flow incl. provenance recording), `list.test.ts`, `src/infra/clawhub.promotions.test.ts` (payload + feed wire-contract validation, conditional fetch/304), `src/infra/promotions-feed.test.ts` (cache round-trip, cadence gate, `If-None-Match` revalidation, sequence monotonicity, offline fail-silent, notified markers, claim provenance upsert), `src/commands/models/list.promotions.test.ts` (promo/ended tags, section rendering, configured suppression, notice-once, expired-window silence). `pnpm test src/commands/models src/commands/promos src/infra/promotions-feed.test.ts src/infra/clawhub.promotions.test.ts` green (125 + infra).
- Gates: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, scoped `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, `oxfmt`, `pnpm docs:check-links`, `pnpm docs:map:check`, full `pnpm build` (no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]`; the promotions decorations load through the same lazy-import boundary as the other `models list` modules).
- Live end-to-end against a local ClawHub instance in an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`: first `models list` fetches the real feed (sequence 27), renders the "Available via promotion" group and the 🎁 notice; second run revalidates nothing (cadence gate), keeps the group, suppresses the notice; the state row holds the ETag, sequence, and notified slugs; `models list --json` contains no promotion text. Claim flow live E2E (auth, registration, default) verified previously on the same instance.
- Structured review (Codex/gpt-5.5) run to a clean final pass on each change bundle; earlier passes' findings (auth completeness, terminal sanitization, window trust, slug/model-ref/identifier contracts, scoped plugin names, plugin install/enable enforcement, runtime repair) are each fixed with regression tests. Two reviewer suggestions were consciously rejected with sibling-contract evidence, documented inline: argv `--api-key` (matches shipped onboard non-interactive flags) and provider-credential reuse (deliberate contract; gated by install provenance and plugin policy).
